from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vectors are arrows from origin to a point.", "We define space with standard basis vectors.", "Unit vectors i and j form the grid."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Points in Space", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid setup
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5], y_range=[-1, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        v = axes.c2p(2, 3)
        vector_v = Arrow(start=axes.c2p(0, 0), end=v, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(vector_v))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        x_label = MathTex("x").next_to(axes.x_axis.get_end(), RIGHT)
        y_label = MathTex("y").next_to(axes.y_axis.get_top(), UP)
        self.add(x_label, y_label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        i_vec = Arrow(start=axes.c2p(0, 0), end=axes.c2p(1, 0), color="#FF00FF", buff=0)
        j_vec = Arrow(start=axes.c2p(0, 0), end=axes.c2p(0, 1), color="#FF00FF", buff=0)
        self.play(Create(i_vec), Create(j_vec))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Matrix as a Transformation Map", [
            "Where do basis vectors land?", 
            "Columns define the transformation map.", 
            "Any vector is a linear combination."
        ])
        
        # Define base vectors and matrix
        matrix = MathTex(r"M = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Write(matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        col_vec_a = MathTex(r"\vec{a} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}", color="#00FF00")
        col_vec_b = MathTex(r"\vec{b} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(col_vec_a, 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(col_vec_b, 'E2')
        self.play(Write(col_vec_a), Write(col_vec_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        vec_x = MathTex(r"x\vec{a} + y\vec{b}", color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(vec_x, 'D5')
        self.play(Write(vec_x))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):

outline.topic: Linear Transformations and Matrices: The Geometry of Change

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Points in Space
sections.content: Briefly define vectors as arrows from the origin (0,0) to a point (x,y). Introduce the standard basis vectors i=(1,0) and j=(0,1) as the 'grid' that defines our space.
sections.example: Visualize a 2D coordinate grid with a 'Robot Scout' standing at (2,3), represented as 2i + 3j.

sections.title: Defining Linear Transformations
sections.content: Explain a transformation as a function T: R² -> R² that moves vectors. Emphasize the two rules: lines remain lines, and the origin remains fixed.
sections.example: An animation showing a 'Grid-Stretcher' machine pulling the grid lines; observe how the Robot Scout moves to a new position while the lines stay perfectly straight.

sections.title: The Matrix as a Transformation Map
sections.content: Introduce the 'Aha!' moment: where do basis vectors i and j land? The columns of a matrix tell us exactly where these vectors end up after the transformation.
sections.example: If i lands at (1, 2) and j lands at (-1, 1), the matrix is [[1, -1], [2, 1]]. Show how any point (x, y) is just x*i_new + y*j_new.

sections.title: Visualizing Common Transformations
sections.content: Demonstrate how specific matrices create specific geometric effects: Rotation (spinning), Scaling (stretching), and Shearing (tilting).
sections.example: A 'Shape-Shifting Fox' animation: Applying a rotation matrix makes the fox spin, while a scaling matrix makes it appear fatter or thinner.

sections.title: Synthesis & Application
sections.content: Summarize that a matrix is not just a grid of numbers, but a specific instruction set for deforming space. This is the foundation of computer graphics and data analysis.
sections.example: Final shot: A 3D wireframe character being manipulated by a matrix, showing how game engines rotate characters by multiplying their vertex coordinates by transformation matrices.
